To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the new constraints on the equation of state from compact star observations can be fulfilled by hybrid stars, and that the transition from hadronic to quark matter in the resulting stiff equation of state is expected to be observable by changes of the cooling and rotational properties of compact stars.

(a) the equation of state is a crucial ingredient for the interpretation of compact star data and the understanding of quark deconfiment in heavy-ion collisions, (b) the high-density behaviour is constrained by the new observations and (c) the occurrence of quarks in compact stars and heavy-ion collisions is possible.

(i) the equation of state is stiff and the deconfinement phase transition in hybrid stars is weakly first-order, (ii) the deconfinment transition in future nucleus–nuclei collisions at the CBM experiment at FAIR can be detected via specific changes in transport phenomena, and (iii) the deconformation transition in future neutron star mergers can be detected via gravitational radiation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a detailed microscopic understanding of the equation of matter in the high-density regime relevant for compact stars.
the investigation of the equation of the state of strongly interacting many-body systems at high densities.
the development of microscopic approaches to quark and hybrid matter and their implications for astrophysics and heavy ion physics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the occurrence of quarks in the interior of compact stars cannot be excluded.
the occurrence of quarks in compact stars cannot be excluded by the new observations, and that the new observations are consistent with the presence of quark matter inside compact stars.

quark matter in the form of colour superconducting quark matter is not excluded by the new data of high-accuracy compact star observations and that the new data provide the basis for a more precise determination of the properties of quark matter and the deconfinement phase transition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the new constraints on the equation of state from compact star observations and the results from quantum field theoretical approaches for quark matter allow a microscopic understanding of compact stars and provide a solid theoretical basis for the search of signals of quark matter formation in compact stars and in heavy-ion collisions.
the new constraints from observations of compact stars and heavy-ion collision experiments can be met by modern microscopic models for quark matter.

the new data on compact star masses and radii have opened up new possibilities for the investigation of the high-density equation of state of quark matter and the phase transition to hadronic matter in terrestrial experiments.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the high-density behaviour in compact stars is a crucial ingredient for the understanding of the structure and evolution of compact objects, and the equation of state is not only determined by the symmetry energy of nuclear matter at normal density but also by the behaviour of the strong interaction at high densities and temperatures.

modern quantum field theories allow to describe compact star observations with a high degree of precision, and that the occurrence of quarks in compact stars is not in conflict with modern observations.
the new, stringent constraints from compact stars can be fulfilled with a stiff hybrid equation of star which is compatible with a deconfined phase in the core.
